models_evaluated: four open-source LLMs (vanilla and RAG configurations; names not given in text)

links.outcome: Answer quality of vanilla LLMs versus retrieval-grounded RAG on consumer health questions (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, LLM and clinical evaluation)
links.effect: Vanilla LLMs consistently outperformed RAG variants on quantitative metrics and qualitative assessments. Retrieval Precision@5 was 0.15. RAG was competitive on scientific consensus and harm reduction.
links.quote: Surprisingly, we find that vanilla LLM approaches consistently outperform RAG variants across both quantitative metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) and qualitative assessments.

screen.reason: Empirically tests whether adding domain-specific retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves LLM responses to consumer health questions compared to vanilla LLMs.
